Title: The Ghost Herd
Rumor: The Ghost Herd. Drovers speak of a great herd of white cattle that crosses the grasslands on moonless nights, attended by a silent rider upon a black horse. No living rancher recognizes the brand burned into their hides, and their hoofprints disappear where the herd crosses the Redwash. Some claim that following them leads to a valley untouched by drought.
First lead: Old drovers at the Redwash Exchange know which bend of the river the herd favors.

Title: The Seven Stone Sisters
Rumor: The Seven Stone Sisters. Seven great standing stones occupy a lonely hill somewhere beyond the established ranchlands. The Rathen claim that each stone marks the burial place of an ancient queen, although no one agrees upon their names. Travelers who camp within the circle report hearing seven women arguing in an unfamiliar tongue. At dawn, one of the stones has sometimes changed position.
First lead: Rathen trailkeepers maintain an old route that passes near the hill.

Title: The Devil's Watering Hole
Rumor: The Devil's Watering Hole. Somewhere among the red hills lies a spring whose waters remain cold and clear even during the worst drought. Animals refuse to drink from it, but desperate travelers claim its waters restore their strength. Several who drank deeply returned home unable to remember their own names.
First lead: A ruined cattle camp beside a dry tributary of the Redwash marks the beginning of an abandoned trail.

Title: The Thunderbird's Bones
Rumor: The Thunderbird's Bones. Varkesh storytellers describe an enormous bird whose wings once brought storms to the grasslands. Its skeleton supposedly lies upon a high sandstone ridge, its ribs large enough for a rider to pass between. When lightning strikes the ridge, the bones are said to shine like polished silver.
First lead: Varkesh herders sometimes point toward the ridge when thunderstorms gather from the uplands.

Title: The Lost Qasari Caravan
Rumor: The Lost Qasari Caravan. An old caravan carrying precious stones, rare spices, and a sealed chest of unknown origin disappeared along a forgotten desert trade route generations ago. According to Qasari tradition, the merchants were not killed, but instead followed a false star into the wilderness. Occasionally, travelers report finding strange silver coins scattered along the route.
First lead: Sahir Keshan has seen coins bearing the caravan master's distinctive mark.

Title: The Orchard Beyond the Grass
Rumor: The Orchard Beyond the Grass. Hunters occasionally discover a grove of ancient fruit trees growing in a sheltered valley far from any settlement. Its fruit ripens in every season, and the ground beneath the trees is said to contain the foundations of a vanished village. Strangest of all, travelers who return to the valley rarely find it in the same place.
First lead: An elderly Rathen storyteller knows a song describing the approach to the valley.

Title: The Horse That Would Not Die
Rumor: The Horse That Would Not Die. The Varkesh tell of a magnificent black stallion that has roamed the plains since before their grandfathers' grandfathers were born. No rope can hold it, no arrow can strike it, and no rider has remained upon its back until sunrise. Some say it is merely a horse of exceptional blood; others claim it once belonged to a forgotten god.
First lead: Varkesh horse breeders occasionally hear reports of a lone black stallion following their herds.

Title: The Weeping Mesa
Rumor: The Weeping Mesa. On certain nights, water runs down the face of an otherwise dry sandstone mesa. Those who approach hear voices calling from within the stone, sometimes speaking the names of people long dead. A Thalenweald account claims that an ancient chamber lies buried beneath the mesa, sealed when the grasslands were still forested.
First lead: Thalenweald wardens know an old trail to the mesa, though few willingly travel it after dark.

Title: The Four Bowls
Rumor: The Four Bowls. Broadmaw giants tell of an ancestral feasting ground where four enormous stone bowls stand upon a hilltop. Every generation, wandering giants leave offerings of cattle, fruit, or bones in the bowls. Those who steal from them are said to be pursued by an immense figure that walks only during thunderstorms.
First lead: Ranchers near the uplands occasionally find enormous footprints leading toward the same distant hill.

Title: The Buried Road
Rumor: The Buried Road. After heavy rain, fragments of a paved road sometimes appear beneath the grass along an old cattle trail. The stones are carved with symbols unfamiliar to the Rathen, Varkesh, and Thalenweald alike. No one knows who built the road, and some travelers insist that the exposed sections lead toward ruins that cannot ordinarily be seen.
First lead: Orun Wheelkeeper knows several places where floodwater has exposed the paving stones.

Title: The Bell Beneath the Prairie
Rumor: The Bell Beneath the Prairie. A deep metallic tolling can sometimes be heard beneath the grasslands shortly before sunrise. Farmers claim the sound comes from an old buried chapel, while others insist it is the ringing of a bell carried by a subterranean river. Wherever the sound originates, livestock become unusually restless before it begins.
First lead: A cluster of abandoned homesteads marks the area where the bell is heard most frequently.

Title: The Painted Cave
Rumor: The Painted Cave. Rathen and Varkesh legends speak of a hidden cavern whose walls bear paintings of enormous beasts, ancient hunts, and unfamiliar stars. Some of the figures appear to move when illuminated by firelight. The oldest paintings reportedly depict people whose descendants have never inhabited the region.
First lead: A Varkesh elder knows the traditional name of the ravine containing the cave.

Title: The Redwash Lights
Rumor: The Redwash Lights. Small blue lights occasionally appear above the river at dusk, drifting upstream against the current. Fishermen say the lights guide the lost toward safe crossings, but a different tradition warns that those who follow them too far vanish into the reeds. Their appearances are most common after violent storms.
First lead: The lights are sometimes visible from the old ford outside Redvale.

Title: The Last Camp of the Bannerless
Rumor: The Last Camp of the Bannerless. Somewhere in the uplands lies the abandoned camp of a company of soldiers who disappeared during the War of Broken Banners. Their cooking fires were reportedly found burning, their equipment neatly arranged, and their horses still tethered, but no bodies were discovered. A few veterans claim the camp contains a locked pay chest that was never recovered.
First lead: Former soldiers sometimes exchange conflicting directions to the camp at the Last Water.

Title: The Stone Rider
Rumor: The Stone Rider. A weathered statue of an armored rider stands upon an isolated hill, though no one remembers erecting it. The rider's face has been worn smooth, and its stone horse points toward the distant mountains. Travelers insist that the statue occasionally turns during the night, and that following its gaze has led prospectors to strange discoveries.
First lead: A herding route through the northern grasslands passes close enough to see the statue from a distance.

Title: The Singing Grass
Rumor: The Singing Grass. There is a broad stretch of prairie where the wind produces a strange, beautiful music. Thalenweald tradition holds that the songs preserve the memories of the land, and that those who listen carefully can hear the voices of its former inhabitants. One traveler claims to have learned the location of a buried treasure from the melody.
First lead: Thalenweald travelers can identify the valley by a distinctive ring of low red hills.

Title: The Silver Antlers
Rumor: The Silver Antlers. Hunters describe a great white stag whose antlers glimmer with silver in the moonlight. It appears only to those traveling alone and always flees toward the same wooded ravine. Some believe it guards an ancient Thalenweald shrine; others insist that the creature is a spirit seeking someone worthy of following it.
First lead: Sightings cluster near the wooded headwaters of a Redwash tributary.

Title: The Hollow Hill
Rumor: The Hollow Hill. A low grassy mound near an abandoned trail sounds strangely hollow when struck. Local children claim a family of little people lives beneath it, emerging at night to borrow tools and return them polished. A few settlers have found strange metal objects near the mound, fashioned with workmanship unlike anything sold in Redvale.
First lead: One of the older homesteads along the trail has a collection of the curious objects.

Title: The Place Where Shadows Point East
Rumor: The Place Where Shadows Point East. Qasari travelers speak of a circle of pale stones that casts shadows toward the rising sun regardless of the hour. The phenomenon supposedly occurs only during certain weeks of the year. Those who understand the arrangement are said to be able to locate a long-forgotten source of water beneath the dry hills.
First lead: An old Qasari route map includes the circle, marked with a warning against disturbing the stones.

Title: The Longhorn King
Rumor: The Longhorn King. Tales persist of an enormous, ancient bull wandering the remotest grasslands, bearing horns wide enough to span a road. Ranchers blame it for broken fences and mysteriously scattered herds, while Varkesh legends describe it as the last descendant of beasts that roamed the plains before the arrival of humans or orcs. No hunter has ever brought back its head.
First lead: A chain of ruined corrals leads toward the remote grazing grounds where it is most often sighted.
